full_judgment:
Mohammad Abdur Rouf. J: Respondent Rahimullah Chowdhury along with his mother filed Title Suit No. 207 of 1997 for permanent injunction against the present petitioners for restraining them from dealing with the trust property and its fund. In that suit the present petitioners as defendants opposed the prayer for temporary injunction by filing a written objection on 27.8.97 disclosing that by an order dated 21.9.96 passed in Misc. Case No. 280 of 1996 under the Trusts Act the learned District Judge. Dhaka had accorded them permission to sell the trust property. Thereafter the respondents procured the certified copy on 17.9.97 of the aforesaid order dated 21.9.96 and filed a revisional application on 7.10.97 under Section 115 C.P.C. against the said order in the High Court Division. It was delayed by 291 days. The High Court Division, however on 7.10.97 issued a Rule. Civil Rule No. 361(Con) of 1997 for condonation of delay which the petitioners opposed by filing a counter affidavit denying material assertions of the present respondent as to the date of his knowledge of the order impugned therein. 

 5. The learned Judge of the High Court Division has held that the present respondent was not a party in the aforesaid Misc. Case and as such he had no knowledge about the order dated 21.9.96 before filing of the aforesaid written objection on 27.8.97, by the present petitioners. Thereafter the respondent obtained on 17.9.97 certified copy of the said order and filed the revisional application on 7.10.97: The learned Judge finally held that the revisional application having been filed within 90 days from the date of knowledge of the impugned order it was well within time. 

 7. In the instant case the learned Judge of the High Court Division on being satisfied with the causes shown by the present respondent having accepted the revisional application there can hardly be any legal grievance of the present petitioners against the impugned judgment of the High Court Division. 

 8. In the facts and circumstances of the case this petition merits no consideration. It is dismissed.
